M1.latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists a finite constant \(C_\varepsilon\) such that, for every \(0<\delta<1\) and every \(f\in L^3(\R^3)\), \[ \|K_\delta f\|_{L^3(S^2)} \le C_\varepsilon\delta^{-\varepsilon} \|f\|_{L^3(\R^3)}. \]
M1.paraphrase: The Kakeya maximal operator over delta-tubes of length 1 is bounded L^3(R^3) -> L^3(S^2) with only a delta^{-eps} loss (the sharp conjectured bound up to eps).
headline_corollaries: Nikodym maximal estimates in R^3 and on constant-curvature 3-manifolds (GLX)
local curved Kakeya estimates under Bourgain's condition (GLX)
M1.relation_to_known_results: Wang-Zahl 2025 proved the set version (Hausdorff/Minkowski dim 3) with a lambda^{K(eps)} shading dependence; WZ state after their Thm 1.2 that lambda^3 would be needed for the maximal conjecture (M1 intro:61-64, per the paper). M1 keeps the GWZ set theorem as a black box and adds the density-sensitive critical-exponent machinery to get lambda^3. Earlier claim: Rios-Sawyer 2506.21315 v1 (June 2025), later retitled to an equivalence result.

M2.latex: Let \(K\subset\R^4\). Suppose that for every \(e\in S^3\) there is a point \(a_e\in\R^4\) such that \[ \{a_e+te:0\leq t\leq1\}\subset K. \] Then \(\dim_H K=4\).
M2.paraphrase: Every (not necessarily measurable or compact) Kakeya set in R^4 has Hausdorff dimension 4.
headline_corollaries: Minkowski and packing dimension 4 for bounded Kakeya sets
dimension bounds for sets with segments in an arbitrary direction set
Nikodym sets on 4D constant-curvature manifolds have full dimension
fixed-chart curved Kakeya dimension; rank-one quadratic curved Kakeya in R^3
M2.relation_to_known_results: Previous best Hausdorff bound in R^4: 3.059 (Katz-Zahl planebrush, corrected v3); maximal parameter 3.0543 (Borges-Chan-Chen-Liu-Xi-Zhan 2511.22824); 3+1/40 polynomial Wolff (Guth-Zahl + Zahl/Katz-Rogers); 13/4 for sticky sets (Rai Choudhuri 2410.23579); Laba-Tao Minkowski >3. M2 does NOT prove the R^4 maximal conjecture. It uses the R^3 set theorem (via M1's weighted plank lemma on projected lines) but none of Wang-Zahl's sticky/grain machinery directly; its engine is new (quadratic charts, horizon, scalar-sheet comparison).

proof_architecture.claim: M1: encode tubes as weighted indexed affine lines with time-bin shadings; set up plank parameters and exponent calculus.
M1: deform the density target into a two-parameter family of critical inequalities with temporal cost Pi_F and plank exponent A; h(p,0)=0 for p->2 gives the theorem via the maximal reduction.
M1: if h(p,0)>0, BV/monotonicity gives an a.e.-differentiable point with h>0, h_z>0; build hybrid and exact equality sequences.

M1: local geometry of equalities: local mass bound, planiness on short blocks (multilinear Kakeya), plate density (Furstenberg) + plate Nikodym => flat delay; saturated plates (GWZ) + anisotropic rescaling => positive deficit.
M1: derivative capture selects saturated shapes; minimum delay + inner/outer cuts force canonical profile beta(s-tau)_+; stationary packets in four moving-frame coordinates.
M1: entropy demand from stationary masses vs projection constraints from two frames on one index (Ren-Wang, product-slope pinning, pair information); five-case closure => h(p,0)=0.
M2: from dim_H K<4, build a version-2 exact problem in C(d), d<1, with positive horizon (uses R^3 set theorem on projected lines via M1's weighted plank lemma).
M2: comparison principle for scalar sheets (two-color matching) => terminal time extension => k>0; optimize d_*, k, narrowness ell into critical paths with linear profiles.

M2: ell=0: isotropic improvement (polynomial field, conservativity, potential) + degree restoration through the hidden coordinate when directions lie near a conic; also gives zero horizon for the scalar model.
M2: 0<ell<inf: scalar projection => wide intervals (improvement) or horizontal Heisenberg-type model; 2k=1 three-leg switch; 2k!=1 bootstrap and return to wide intervals.
M2: ell=inf excluded by full-time localization and scalar projection; all regimes contradict extremality, so dim_H K=4.
Corollaries via cited transfers (Nikodym, curved Kakeya, direction sets, Minkowski/packing).

Wang-Zahl/GWZ is used as a black-box set theorem valid only for lambda >= delta^eta; everything that handles low-density shadings is new to M1: temporal deficit profile and cost Pi_F, deformed critical exponent h(p,z), derivative capture, flat delay, canonical profile, moving-frame entropy rates, product-slope pinning, five-case closure.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap located, but verification was far from complete. Both manuscripts are unrefereed, unformalised and extremely compressed (M1 7,446 lines; M2 14,184 lines). Arithmetic and logical spot checks on M1 pass. M2 jumps from the best known 3.059 to 4 in one paper, an extraordinary claim. Treat both as unverified.

M2: introduction in full, Sec 2 framework 1-95/330-470/855-967/1155-1420, Sec 3 1-45/270-340, Sec 4 1-135, Sec 5 360-410, Sec 6 1-75/1360-1400/1565-1600, Sec 6a 300-330, Sec 7 1-45/900-960, Sec 8 1-100, Sec 9 1-60 and completion; about 2,100 of 14,184 lines (~15%), all 82 theorem-like statements read.

residual_concerns: Dependence on GWZ 2601.14411 Thm 1.1 (both manuscripts). Public signals, snippet-level only and unverified: Alex Cohen's NYU notes following GWZ say 'There are some technical issues in Section 5'; Hua-Yang (arXiv 2608.18870, v2 titled 'a Repair', v3 'a Conditional Repair of the Streamlined Three-Dimensional Kakeya Reduction') report a compatibility problem in GWZ's maximal-density factorization with only a conditional fix; a Zenodo note (Zeraoulia) lists 'technical corrections'. The original Wang-Zahl 2502.17655 (with lambda^{K(eps)} and lambda>=delta^eta) probably supplies the same input, but its convex-Wolff hypotheses were not checked against M1's convex-clustering form.
